title: Joint Statement by Human Rights Organizations regarding Abduction of Human Rights Defenders
content:
We, the undersigned organizations, condemn in strongest possible terms the abduction of three human rights defenders by Vietnamese authorities in Cambodia and their subsequent arbitrary detention in Vietnam.

The Vietnamese government must immediately and unconditionally release Nguyen Duc Thuan, a Norwegian citizen, Tran Hiep (Ho Pham Hiep Huy), an Australian citizen, and Thai Cong Truong Son, an ethnic Vietnamese living in Cambodia. Pending their release, Norwegian and Australian consular officials must be granted immediate access to Mr. Thuan and Mr. Hiep.

Background

Mr. Thuan and Mr. Hiep went missing on the morning of 18 September 2026 while traveling to the Kaoh Andaet area of Cambodia. For ten days, they were incommunicado.

On 28 September, Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security announced that the three men had been caught “illegally entering Vietnam” at the My Quy Tay Border Gate on 18 September. Subsequently, the three men are currently being investigated for “terrorism”. Their families and colleagues strongly reject this account. All available information points to the fact that the men were abducted on Cambodian soil and forcibly taken across the border.

title: The Belarusian People Deserve to be Free: Remarks by Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly
content:
Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly joined Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, the leader of Belarus’s democratic movement, along with senior officials from the European Union, the Council of Europe, Estonia, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Sweden, and Ukraine for a UN General Assembly side event focused on the threat that Lukashenka’s autocratic regime poses to regional and international security. 

His remarks, addressing Lukashenka’s repression, Freedom House’s role in assisting Belarusian political prisoners, and the importance of a free and democratic Belarus, follow.

Jamie Fly: It’s an honor to be here today with so many staunch transatlantic allies of the United States and strong advocates for freedom, including Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, whose leadership and continued advocacy on behalf of the Belarusian people is critical to the country’s democratic future.

title: Political Prisoners Watch: Five Democracy Advocates Targeted for Seeking Help Abroad
content:
From left to right: Pham Chi Dung, Anar Mammadli, Joshua Wong, Mohammad Seifzadeh, Gasser Abdel Razek (Photo Credits: Pham Chi Dung Facebook, Wikimedia Commons, Center for Human Rights in Iran, Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights)

On September 2, prominent Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to charges under the territory’s notorious National Security Act—the second time he has faced prison time under the Beijing-imposed law. Having already been imprisoned since November 2020, he now faces the possibility of another lengthy sentence simply for demanding that Hong Kongers have a voice in their own government. Joshua’s detention has been widely recognized as emblematic of the Chinese Communist Party’s increasing restrictions on freedom in and the autonomy of Hong Kong.

title: Xi Jinping in Washington, DC: Countering Beijing’s Efforts to Undermine Free Speech Beyond Its Borders
content:
US President Donald Trump greets Chinese Communist Party General Secretary Xi Jinping before a bilateral meeting in 2025 in South Korea. (Photo Credit: The White House/Daniel Torok)

On September 24, President Trump plans to hold a White House State Dinner in Washington, DC, for Chinese Communist Party (CCP) General Secretary Xi Jinping. Much of the media coverage is likely to highlight trade, security, technology, and strategic competition; however, the US government has both a moral and national security obligation to forcefully condemn the CCP’s human rights abuses at home and its efforts to extend repression and restrictions on free speech abroad.

Just as importantly, given the CCP’s extensive record of transnational repression and authoritarian coercion abroad, federal and local authorities should protect the rights of the demonstrators expected to peacefully protest Xi’s visit on US soil and ensure that Beijing is not permitted to export the restrictions on dissent commonly seen in China.

title: The CCP is Trying—and Failing—to Extinguish Defiance among Chinese Citizens
content:
Demonstrators in Chongqing protest animal abuse with large numbers of police on the scene (Photo Credit: HK01).

Recent propaganda and censorship efforts by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) have revealed an urgent desire among party leadership to blunt a spirit of defiance within Chinese society. Despite the party’s attempts to curb dissent, however, China’s citizens continue to defy authority, as evidenced by recent findings of Freedom House’s China Dissent Monitor (CDM). 

Earlier this year, China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) conducted a campaign that blamed “foreign forces” for funding the spread in China of “lying flat” (躺平), a term that has become widely used to describe the rejection of societal expectations that push individuals to strive for material and social achievement. The official media attributing the trend of lying flat to foreign interference was promptly pilloried by Chinese netizens who filled online comment sections with criticism and satire. A popular vlogger sarcastically complained that he wanted to “report” foreign forces for failing to pay him despite his tireless efforts to lie flat. These responses have all since been censored.

title: 25+ Civil Society Organizations Call for Strong Human Rights and Accountability Safeguards for Commercial Cyber Intrusion Industry
content:
Download the full statement


The joint statement from civil society argues that the forthcoming Pall Mall Industry Guidelines on Commercial Cyber Intrusion Capabilities (CCICs), which includes commercial spyware, must establish enforceable expectations for governments and companies, and significantly raise the bar on existing industry practices.

The Guidelines are a historic opportunity to make accountability the new norm, but weak or diluted language could instead legitimize an industry associated with serious human-rights abuses.

Some highlights from the joint statement include:

  • CCICs pose exceptional human-rights risks.
    Technologies such as commercial spyware can facilitate grave and potentially irreversible violations, including arbitrary surveillance, detention and transnational repression.
  • Exceptional risks require exceptional safeguards and limitations. The use of spyware cannot be normalized.
    The Guidelines should impose heavy restrictions and controls that drastically limit access and use, ensure oversight, embed accountability and facilitate remediation.
creator: zevans@freedomhouse.org

title: An Open Letter to Chinese Communist Party General Secretary Xi Jinping
content:
Re: Human rights improvements ahead of September 24, 2026 visit to Washington, DC

We, the undersigned organizations dedicated to protecting and promoting human rights, democracy, and religious freedom, write on the occasion of your forthcoming visit to Washington, DC.  We urge that ahead of your arrival you agree to release prisoners of conscience, pledge an end to transnational repression, and commit to critical legal reforms, among other actions. Such steps would diminish criticism around the visit of your government’s human rights violations.

title: China: Ensure Sophia Huang Xueqin’s Release and Guarantee Her Freedom from Arbitrary Restrictions
content:
As journalist and prominent #MeToo activist Sophia Huang Xueqin approaches the end of her unjust five-year prison sentence, we, the undersigned civil society organizations, call on the Chinese authorities to ensure her immediate release and guarantee that, once released, she can carry out her journalism and human rights work without surveillance, harassment, retaliation or other restrictions.

Sophia Huang Xueqin is widely recognized for her work on human rights and commitment to press freedom. She is a journalist and one of the most prominent figures associated with China’s #MeToo movement. For years, she reported on and advocated for gender equality and supported survivors of sexual harassment and gender-based violence.

In September 2021, Sophia was preparing to start graduate studies in the UK. However, she and a friend, human and labour rights activist Wang Jianbing, were arrested in Guangzhou, China on 19 September, and detained incommunicado for more than five months. While in detention, both Sophia and Jianbing were reportedly subjected to ill-treatment, with negative impacts on their health.

title: Freedom House Launches Ambassadors for Freedom Program, Names Five Leading Human Rights Defenders as Inaugural Advocates
content:
WASHINGTON—Today Freedom House launched the Ambassadors for Freedom program, a new global initiative bringing together a group of the world’s foremost democracy advocates to champion solutions to the 20-year decline in global freedom. Carolina Barrero, Nazanin Boniadi, Anaïse Kanimba, Vladimir Kara-Murza, and Anna Kwok will serve as the inaugural ambassadors. Ambassadors will work in partnership with Freedom House to spotlight threats to freedom, engage policymakers and the public, and inspire a new generation to safeguard democracy.

“Freedom House has always believed that lasting change is driven by courageous individuals willing to stand up for freedom, often at great personal cost,” said Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly. “These ambassadors are some of the world’s great champions of the power of freedom and speak from personal experience as targets of repressive regimes themselves. Their courage is an example to us all and we are thrilled to welcome them as Freedom House Ambassadors.”
